# Nexora Docs — full text
Developer: Mohamed Hamra (محمد حمرة) — https://github.com/mhamad-code

## Welcome to Nexora — Your Android AI Chat Application
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/introduction.html
Nexora is a native Android app that unifies OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, and any OpenAI-compatible provider in one beautiful interface.

 Nexora brings every major AI provider together in a single, polished Android app. Instead of juggling separate apps and browser tabs, you connect your own API keys once and chat with OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — all from the same familiar interface. Nexora is built natively in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose, so it feels fast, responsive, and right at home on your Android device. Get Started Download Nexora Install Nexora from GitHub Releases and get set up in minutes. Quickstart Add your first provider, pick a model, and send your first message in under five minutes. AI Providers Connect OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible API. Assistants Create custom assistants with tailored system prompts, models, and personas. MCP Extensions Extend Nexora's capabilities with Model Context Protocol plugins and tools. Web Access Open Nexora's chat interface from a browser on your local network. Why Nexora? Nexora was designed around one idea: you should own your AI experience. You bring your own API keys, choose your own models, and keep your conversations private. There are no subscriptions, no middlemen, and no lock-in. Multiple Providers, One App Switch between OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI-compatible APIs without leaving the app. Custom Assistants Build reusable assistants with custom system prompts, model selections, and personalities. MCP Tool Support Connect external tools and data sources through the Model Context Protocol. Live Web Search Enable real-time web access so your AI answers stay accurate and up to date. Nexora is based on RikkaHub (AGPL-3.0). This documentation is adapted from the RikkaHub documentation, which is published under the MIT license — see LICENSE . 

## Install Nexora on Android
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/download.html
Download the Nexora APK from GitHub Releases, pick the build that matches your device, and complete the first-launch setup.

 Nexora is a native Android application distributed as an APK from the project's GitHub Releases page. This page walks you through downloading, installing, and completing your first launch. System Requirements Nexora runs on Android smartphones and tablets. There is no iOS version. Download Open the Releases page Go to the Nexora Releases page in your browser. Pick the right file Each release contains several APK files: File When to use it app-arm64-v8a-release.apk Most modern phones (64-bit processor). app-armeabi-v7a-release.apk Older phones with a 32-bit processor. app-x86_64-release.apk Emulators and devices with an x86 chip. app-universal-release.apk Works on all of the above, but the file is larger. If you are not sure which one fits your device, use the universal build. Install the APK Open the downloaded file from your file manager. If prompted, allow Install unknown apps for your browser or file manager, then follow the on-screen prompts. Only download Nexora from the official repository linked above. APKs from other sources may be outdated or tampered with. To update, install a newer APK over the existing app. Releases are signed with the same key, so your data is kept. First Launch Experience Once Nexora is installed, open it from your home screen or app drawer. The first time you launch the app, Nexora walks you through the essential setup: Welcome Screen Nexora greets you with a brief welcome screen. Tap Get Started to move to the setup flow. Add a Provider Nexora prompts you to add at least one AI provider. Select your preferred provider — OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint — and enter your API key. You can add more providers later from Settings → Providers . Choose a Default Model Pick a default model for new conversations. You can always change the model on a per-conversation basis. Start Chatting Tap Start Chatting to open the main conversation view. Nexora is ready to use. Import Provider Settings via QR Code If you have already configured Nexora on another device, you can skip manual API key entry by importing your provider settings with a QR code. How to import via QR code On your existing device: Open Settings → Providers . Tap the Export or Share option and choose QR Code . A QR code containing your provider configuration is displayed on screen. On your new device: Complete installation and open Nexora. On the provider setup screen, tap Import via QR Code . Point your camera at the QR code 

## Quickstart: Send Your First AI Message in 5 Minutes
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/quickstart.html
Install Nexora on Android, connect your first AI provider with your API key, choose a model, and send your first message in under five minutes.

 This guide gets you from zero to your first AI conversation as quickly as possible. You need an Android device, a copy of Nexora installed, and an API key from at least one AI provider. If you do not have an API key yet, sign up with your chosen provider first — links are included in the steps below. Download and Install Nexora Install Nexora on your Android device from the project's GitHub Releases page. Nexora Releases (GitHub) Download the latest APK from the project's GitHub Releases page. Once installation is complete, open Nexora from your home screen or app drawer. Open Settings and Add a Provider Nexora needs at least one AI provider before you can chat. Navigate to the provider settings now. Tap the Settings icon (gear) at the bottom of the sidebar. Select Provider Settings from the settings menu. Many providers are pre-configured — if yours is listed, just tap it and enter your API key. If not, tap the button in the top-right corner to create a new provider. OpenAI Google Gemini Anthropic Claude The most widely used API format. Enter the base URL and API key from your provider to complete the setup. OpenAI has two API versions. Chat Completions is the default in Nexora and is the most popular format supported by the vast majority of providers. The newer Responses API is what OpenAI itself now prioritizes — if you are using the official OpenAI API or a relay that mirrors GPT models, switching to the Responses API is recommended. Tap Use Responses API to enable it. Google's own API format, used exclusively for Google Gemini models. The second most widely adopted API format after OpenAI. Used by Claude and a number of other models as well. Enter Your API Key Paste your API key into the API Key field for the provider you selected. If you are using an unofficial relay that is not built into Nexora, you will also need to set the provider's Base URL when creating a new provider. Treat your API key like a password. Do not share it, and do not paste it into untrusted apps. Nexora stores your key locally on your device and never sends it to Nexora's servers — it goes directly to your chosen provider. After pasting your key, tap Save or Confirm to store the provider configuration. Add Models After configuring a provider, scroll to the Models section at the bottom of the provider screen and tap it. Most providers support fetching the model list automatically — tap the expand button to load the list, then select the models you want to use. To remove a model 

## AI Providers — Connect to Your Preferred AI Services
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/providers/overview.html
Learn how to add, configure, and switch between multiple AI providers in Nexora, including OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, and custom endpoints.

 Nexora lets you connect to multiple AI services at the same time, so you can pick the right model for every conversation without leaving the app. Each connection you configure is called a provider — it stores the API key, base URL, and any additional options needed to talk to a specific AI service. You can add as many providers as you like, enable or disable them individually, and switch between their models directly from the chat screen. Supported provider types Nexora ships with first-class support for three provider types and a flexible custom option that works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. OpenAI Connect to OpenAI's API — including GPT-4o, o-series reasoning models, and the Responses API — or any service that mirrors the Chat Completions endpoint. Google Gemini Access Gemini models directly through the Google AI API, or use Vertex AI with a service account for enterprise deployments. Anthropic Claude Chat with Claude models via the Anthropic API, with optional prompt caching to reduce latency and cost on long conversations. Custom / OpenAI-compatible Point Nexora at OpenRouter, a local Ollama instance, a self-hosted proxy, or any other service that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol. Add your first provider Open Settings Tap the Settings icon in the bottom navigation bar to open the settings screen. Go to Providers Select Providers from the settings list to see all configured providers. Add a provider Tap Add Provider , choose a provider type, fill in your API key and any other required fields, then save. Add models Inside the provider detail screen, add the model IDs you want to use. Each model appears in the model picker when you start or switch a conversation. Manage multiple providers You can configure as many providers as you need. Use the toggle on each provider card to enable or disable it without deleting your settings. Disabled providers and their models are hidden from the model picker. If you want to compare responses from different providers, add each one separately and switch models between conversations — no re-entering credentials required. Share provider configs with QR codes Every provider detail screen has a Share button that encodes your provider configuration (API key, base URL, and settings — without any added models) into a QR code. Another Nexora user can scan that QR code to import the same provider setup instantly. You can also copy the encoded string and send it over any messaging app. The QR code and share st

## OpenAI Provider — GPT, o-series, and Compatible APIs
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/providers/openai.html
Set up an OpenAI provider in Nexora to use GPT-4o, o-series reasoning models, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with full API key and URL control.

 The OpenAI provider type connects Nexora to OpenAI's Chat Completions or Responses API. Because the OpenAI protocol has become an industry standard, this same provider type also works with dozens of third-party services — simply change the base URL. This page focuses on a direct OpenAI connection; for third-party and local setups, see Custom / OpenAI-compatible providers . Add an OpenAI provider Open provider settings Go to Settings → Providers and tap Add Provider . Choose OpenAI Select OpenAI from the provider type list. Enter your API key Paste your OpenAI API key into the API Key field. You can find or create keys at platform.openai.com/api-keys . Confirm the base URL The base URL defaults to https://api.openai.com/v1 . Leave it unchanged for a standard OpenAI connection. Add models Tap Add Model , enter the model ID (for example gpt-4o or o3 ), set its display name and capabilities, then save. Repeat for each model you want to use. Save Tap Save to apply your changes. The provider and its models now appear in the model picker. Configuration reference Core fields apiKey string required Your OpenAI API key. Nexora stores it locally on your device and sends it only to the configured base URL. Supports comma-separated key rotation (for example sk-key1,sk-key2 ) when you have multiple keys. baseUrl string default: https://api.openai.com/v1 The root URL of the OpenAI-compatible API. Change this when connecting to a proxy or a third-party service that mirrors the OpenAI API. chatCompletionsPath string default: /chat/completions The path appended to the base URL for chat requests. Override this only if your provider uses a non-standard path. Advanced fields useResponseApi boolean default: false Switch from the Chat Completions endpoint to OpenAI's newer Responses API. Enable this for models that only support the Responses API, such as those served by xAI's Grok endpoint. includeHistoryReasoning boolean default: true When enabled, Nexora includes the reasoning_content from previous assistant turns when sending conversation history. Disable this if your provider rejects messages containing reasoning fields. Balance checking Enable balance checking to display your remaining API credit directly in the provider detail screen. balanceOption.enabled boolean default: false Turn on the balance display for this provider. balanceOption.apiPath string default: /credits The path (relative to the base URL) or full URL used to fetch your balance. Common values: /credits — 

## Google Gemini Provider — Set Up Gemini and Vertex AI
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/providers/google.html
Connect Nexora to Google's Gemini models using the Gemini API or Vertex AI with a service account for enterprise and private cloud deployments.

 The Google provider type connects Nexora to Google's generative AI platform. You can use either the public Gemini API — the quickest option for personal use — or Vertex AI with a Google Cloud service account for enterprise or private-cloud deployments. Both paths support the full range of Gemini models including Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Add a Google provider Open provider settings Go to Settings → Providers and tap Add Provider . Choose Google Select Google from the provider type list. Enter your API key Paste your Gemini API key into the API Key field. You can create a free key at aistudio.google.com/app/apikey . Leave this field empty if you are using a Vertex AI service account instead. Confirm the base URL The base URL defaults to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta . Leave it unchanged for the standard Gemini API. Add Gemini models Tap Add Model , enter the model ID (for example gemini-2.5-pro or gemini-2.5-flash ), set its display name and capabilities, then save. Save Tap Save to apply your changes. Configuration reference Core fields apiKey string required Your Gemini API key from Google AI Studio. Required when Vertex AI is disabled. If you are authenticating via a Vertex AI service account, leave this blank and fill in the service account fields instead. baseUrl string default: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta The root URL of the Google generative language API. Change this only if you are routing requests through a custom proxy. Vertex AI Enable Vertex AI to route requests through your Google Cloud project instead of the public Gemini API. Vertex AI gives you VPC-SC controls, data-residency guarantees, and enterprise SLAs. vertexAI boolean default: false Switch from the public Gemini API to Google Cloud Vertex AI. When enabled, you must also configure the service account fields below. useServiceAccount boolean default: false Authenticate to Vertex AI using a Google Cloud service account rather than a simple API key. Requires the four service account fields below. privateKey string The PEM-encoded private key from your service account JSON file. Copy the value of the private_key field, including the -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- and -----END PRIVATE KEY----- delimiters. Only required when Use Service Account is enabled. serviceAccountEmail string The client_email value from your service account JSON file (for example my-sa@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com ). Only required when Use Service Account is enable

## Anthropic Claude Provider — All Claude Model Tiers
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/providers/claude.html
Configure Anthropic Claude in Nexora to access Claude models, with optional prompt caching to reduce latency and costs on long conversations.

 The Claude provider type connects Nexora directly to Anthropic's API. In addition to the standard connection options, Nexora exposes Anthropic's prompt caching feature, which stores repeated prefix content (such as long system prompts or document contexts) between turns so the API does not re-process them on every request. This can significantly reduce both cost and time-to-first-token on lengthy conversations. Add a Claude provider Open provider settings Go to Settings → Providers and tap Add Provider . Choose Claude Select Claude from the provider type list. Enter your API key Paste your Anthropic API key into the API Key field. Create or manage keys at console.anthropic.com/settings/keys . Confirm the base URL The base URL defaults to https://api.anthropic.com/v1 . Leave it unchanged for a direct Anthropic connection. Configure prompt caching (optional) If you want to reduce API costs on long conversations, enable Prompt Caching and choose a TTL. Add Claude models Tap Add Model , enter a model ID (for example claude-opus-4-5 or claude-sonnet-4-5 ), set its display name and capabilities, then save. Save Tap Save to apply your changes. Configuration reference Core fields apiKey string required Your Anthropic API key. Nexora stores it locally and sends it only to the configured base URL using the x-api-key header as required by the Anthropic API. baseUrl string default: https://api.anthropic.com/v1 The root URL for the Anthropic API. Change this only if you are routing traffic through a proxy or an Anthropic-compatible third-party endpoint. Prompt caching Anthropic's prompt caching saves the KV cache of a message prefix on their servers, so subsequent turns that re-send the same prefix are billed at a reduced cache-read rate and return faster. promptCaching boolean default: false Enable prompt caching for this provider. When turned on, Nexora marks eligible message prefixes with the cache_control field in the API request. promptCacheTtl enum default: FIVE_MINUTES How long Anthropic retains the cached prefix on their servers. Value Duration When to use FIVE_MINUTES 5 minutes Short to medium conversations where cache reuse is likely within the same session ONE_HOUR 1 hour Long research or coding sessions where you return to the same context repeatedly Prompt caching is available on Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Claude 3 Opus, and newer models. Check docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching for full eligibility details and pricing. 

## Custom Providers — OpenAI-Compatible APIs and Local Models
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/providers/custom.html
Connect Nexora to any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint, including OpenRouter, local Ollama, self-hosted proxies, and other third-party services.

 Nexora's OpenAI provider type is not limited to OpenAI itself. Because the OpenAI Chat Completions API has become a universal standard, you can point it at virtually any compatible service — model aggregators such as OpenRouter, a local Ollama instance running entirely on your device or home network, a corporate proxy, or any self-hosted open-source inference server. All you need to do is create an OpenAI provider, swap the base URL, and add the model IDs your endpoint exposes. Connect to a custom endpoint Add an OpenAI provider Go to Settings → Providers , tap Add Provider , and select OpenAI . Change the base URL Replace the default https://api.openai.com/v1 with the base URL of your service. See the examples below for common endpoints. Enter your API key Paste the API key your service issued. Some local services (such as Ollama) do not require a key — you can enter any placeholder value such as ollama in that case. Add custom headers (if needed) Some services require extra HTTP headers. Open the Custom Headers section and add any required key-value pairs. Add models Tap Add Model and enter the model IDs your endpoint supports. For aggregators like OpenRouter, use the full model slug (for example openai/gpt-4o or anthropic/claude-opus-4-5 ). Save Tap Save . Your custom provider is now available in the model picker. Popular endpoint examples OpenRouter Route requests to 100+ models from multiple providers through a single API key. Base URL: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 Required headers: HTTP-Referer : your app or website URL (identifies your app to OpenRouter) X-Title : a short display name for your app (optional but recommended) Ollama (local) Run open-source models entirely on your device or local network — no API key required. Base URL: http://localhost:11434/v1 API Key: any non-empty string, for example ollama Start Ollama and pull a model ( ollama pull llama3.2 ) before adding it in Nexora. LM Studio (local) Serve local GGUF models from your PC to your Android device over your home network. Base URL: http://YOUR_PC_IP:1234/v1 API Key: lm-studio (or any placeholder) Custom proxy Route requests through your own server for key management, logging, or rate limiting. Base URL: your proxy URL, for example https://my-proxy.example.com/v1 Add any authentication headers your proxy requires in Custom Headers . Custom HTTP headers Open the Custom Headers section inside the provider detail screen to add arbitrary HTTP headers to every request this provider send

## Managing Conversations in the Nexora Chat Interface
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/chat/conversations.html
Start chats, switch models, edit and regenerate messages, render rich Markdown, favorite content, share, and track token usage in Nexora.

 The chat screen is where you spend most of your time in Nexora. Every conversation is stored locally on your device, and you can create as many as you need across multiple AI providers without any limit imposed by the app. Starting a New Conversation Tap the compose icon (pencil-and-paper) in the top-right corner of the chat toolbar to open a fresh conversation. Nexora automatically generates a title for the conversation once you send your first message. You can rename it at any time by tapping the title in the top bar — an inline edit dialog will appear. Open the chat screen Launch Nexora. The last conversation you used opens automatically. Tap the new-chat icon Tap the MessageAdd icon in the top-right corner. A blank conversation opens immediately. Type your message and send Enter your text in the input bar at the bottom and tap the send button (arrow-up). Nexora streams the reply in real time. Switching Between Conversations All your past conversations live in the history drawer . On phones, swipe from the left edge or tap the hamburger menu icon to open the drawer. On large-screen devices (tablets and foldables in landscape), the drawer is always visible on the left side. Inside the drawer you will find: A search bar that jumps to the conversation search page where you can search message content across all chats using full-text search. A History shortcut that takes you to the full conversation list. The conversation list itself, sorted by most recently updated, with pinned items at the top. Tap any conversation to switch to it. Long-press a conversation item to reveal context menu options such as rename, pin, move to a different assistant, or delete. Pin frequently used conversations by long-pressing them in the drawer and selecting Pin . Pinned conversations always appear at the top of the list. Switching Models Mid-Conversation You can change the active AI model at any point without starting a new chat. Tap the model selector shown below the conversation title in the top bar (or inside the input bar on some screen sizes). A picker lists all models from every provider you have configured. Select a new model — subsequent messages will use it while earlier messages remain unchanged. Switching models does not re-generate any previous messages. Only new messages sent after the switch use the newly selected model. Regenerating and Editing Messages Nexora lets you refine any exchange without losing context. Regenerate a Response Long-press an assistant mes

## Multimodal Input: Attach Images and Documents to Chats
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/chat/multimodal.html
Attach images, PDFs, DOCX files, and more to your Nexora messages. Learn how OCR and document extraction work for non-vision models.

 Nexora supports more than plain text. You can attach images, documents, and other files directly to any message, and the app handles the conversion steps needed to deliver that content to the underlying AI model — whether the model natively understands images or not. Attaching Files Tap the + (Add) button on the left side of the chat input bar to open the attachment picker. From there you can choose how to add content: Camera Take a photo on the spot. The image is saved to app storage and attached immediately. Gallery / Files Pick one or more images or documents from your device. Supported document types include PDF, DOCX, PPTX, and EPUB. Paste from clipboard Copy an image from another app, tap the input field, and paste. Nexora detects the image and attaches it automatically. Share from another app Use Android's share sheet to send a file or image to Nexora. The shared content pre-populates the input bar ready to send. Attached files appear as chips above the text input. Tap the × on any chip to remove that attachment before sending. Images When you attach an image and the selected model supports vision input, Nexora encodes the image as base64 and passes it directly to the model. The model sees the image as part of the conversation. Attachment chips for images display a small thumbnail so you can confirm the right file is attached before sending. Not all models support image input. If you select a model that does not accept image modalities, Nexora automatically falls back to OCR — see the OCR section below. Documents: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, and EPUB Nexora supports the following document types natively: Format Extension MIME type PDF .pdf application/pdf Word .docx application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document PowerPoint .pptx application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation E-book .epub application/epub+zip When you attach a supported document, Nexora extracts its text content before the message is sent. The extracted text is injected as a text block at the beginning of your message, formatted like this: ## user sent a file: report.pdf [content] [extracted text goes here] [/content] The model then reads the document text as part of your prompt, letting you ask questions about the content, summarise it, or request translations — even if the model has no native file-upload capability. Very large documents may exceed a model's context window. If you receive an error about context length, try sending a shorter 

## Conversation Branching: Explore Alternate Chat Paths
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/chat/branching.html
Fork any conversation at a specific message to explore different answers, compare models, or A/B test prompts — all without losing prior context.

 Branching lets you diverge a conversation from any point and explore a different direction without overwriting what came before. Every branch shares the full message history up to the split point, so the AI always has the context it needs. What Branching Is Every message in Nexora is stored inside a message node . A node can hold multiple versions of the same message — for example, the original assistant reply and one or more regenerated alternatives. When you regenerate a response, a new version is added to the same node, and you can swipe left and right through the versions at that position without affecting any other part of the conversation. A fork (also called a branch) is something bigger: it creates a brand-new conversation that starts with a copy of every message up to and including the message you forked from. Both the original conversation and the fork are independent — editing one does not affect the other. Creating a Branch Find the message you want to fork from Scroll to any message in the conversation — it can be a user message or an assistant reply. Open the message action menu Long-press the message, or tap the overflow (three-dot) menu that appears below it. Tap Fork Select Fork from the action menu. Nexora copies all messages up to and including the selected one into a new conversation and navigates you there immediately. Continue from the fork point You are now in a fresh conversation that picks up exactly where the fork was made. Send a different prompt, change the model, or adjust the assistant settings — none of these changes affect the original conversation. Navigating Between Versions on the Same Node When a message node has more than one version (created by Regenerate or Edit ), a small branch navigator appears inline with that message. It shows the current version number and the total, for example 2 / 3 . Tap the left arrow (←) to go to the previous version. Tap the right arrow (→) to go to the next version. The arrows dim when you are already at the first or last version. All subsequent messages in the conversation update automatically to reflect the selected branch of history — Nexora always shows the path formed by the currently selected version at each node. Use branching to A/B test prompts or compare how different models answer the same question. Fork the conversation at your user message, switch models, and send the same question — then compare both forks side by side. How Branched Conversations Are Stored Shared history u

## Web Search: Ground AI Answers in Live Search Results
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/chat/search.html
Enable Nexora's built-in web search to inject real-time results into any conversation, configure your preferred search service, and use the Search page.

 Nexora includes a built-in web search capability that lets any AI model access live information from the web. When you enable web search before sending a message, Nexora automatically calls your configured search service, retrieves relevant results, and injects them into the conversation context before the model generates its reply. Enabling Web Search for a Message The web search toggle lives in the input toolbar — the row of icons just above the text field. Tap the search toggle Tap the globe or search icon in the toolbar to enable web search. The icon highlights to indicate it is active. Type your message Write your question or prompt as normal. You do not need to phrase it differently — Nexora extracts the search query automatically. Send the message Tap send. Nexora calls the search service, retrieves results, and injects them as context before asking the model to respond. You will see a brief processing indicator while the search is in progress. Review the cited sources The assistant's reply includes references to the search results. Tap any linked URL to open it in your browser. Web search is powered by a tool call injected into the conversation. The model decides when to invoke the search_web tool based on your prompt. If the model determines that search is unnecessary for a given question, it may skip the web call and answer from its training data. Supported Search Services Nexora supports a wide range of search providers. Configure one or more and select which one to use as the active service. General purpose AI-powered Scraping & crawling Specialised Service Notes Bing Uses the Microsoft Bing Search API. No additional configuration required beyond an API key. Brave Privacy-focused search via the Brave Search API. SearXNG Self-hosted meta-search engine. Provide your instance URL, optional credentials, and preferred search engines. Bocha Chinese-language search service with optional AI-generated summaries. Metaso Chinese AI-powered search service. Service Notes Tavily AI search API optimised for LLM use. Supports general , news , and finance topic modes, plus standard/advanced depth. Exa Semantic search API built for AI applications. Perplexity Uses Perplexity's search-augmented models. Optional max-tokens settings for replies and per-page content. LinkUp Configurable search depth (standard / deep). Grok xAI's Grok model with live web search. Supports custom API URL, model choice, and a configurable system prompt. Tinyfish Lightweight AI search s

## Assistants: Personas, Models, and Settings
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/assistants/overview.html
Create and manage reusable AI personas that bundle a system prompt, model choice, and generation settings into a single switchable profile.

 Assistants are saved configurations that give the AI a distinct identity and behaviour. Each assistant stores a system prompt, an optional model override, generation parameters, and a host of advanced options — so you can switch between a coding helper, a creative writing partner, and a language tutor with a single tap, without reconfiguring anything. Creating an assistant Open Settings Tap the settings icon from the main screen to open the Settings menu. Navigate to Assistants Select Assistants from the list. Add a new assistant Tap the + button in the top-right corner. Enter a name for your assistant, then tap Save . Configure the assistant Tap the newly created assistant card to open its detail pages and fill in the fields described below. Importing a SillyTavern character card Nexora can import character cards in the standard SillyTavern format, giving you instant access to community-created personas without any manual setup. Open the creation sheet Tap the + button on the Assistants screen. Choose your file format Tap Import Tavern PNG to pick a character card image, or Import Tavern JSON to pick a JSON file. Confirm the import Nexora reads the embedded metadata, builds the system prompt automatically, and saves the assistant — including the card artwork as the chat background. Nexora supports character card spec versions v2 and v3 . Importing a card automatically populates the name, system prompt, description, personality, scenario, and first message. Basic configuration Identity Set the assistant's name and avatar to make it easy to recognise at a glance. Enable Use Assistant Avatar to display the assistant's avatar in place of the model icon inside the chat. Model override Set a Chat Model to pin this assistant to a specific provider and model. Leave it blank to use whatever model is currently selected as the global default. System prompt Write the core instructions that define how the assistant thinks and responds. The system prompt is sent at the beginning of every conversation. You can use placeholder variables inside the system prompt. Tags Assign tags to organise your assistants. Use the tag filter bar on the Assistants screen to quickly find the one you need. Key settings reference Generation settings temperature float | null default: null Controls response randomness. Values range from 0 (deterministic) to 2 (very creative). Leave unset to use the model's default. topP float | null default: null Nucleus sampling threshold. A lower value res

## Assistant Memory: Persistent Facts Across Chats
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/assistants/memory.html
Enable AI memory so Nexora remembers key facts about you across conversations, and learn how to view, edit, and scope those memories.

 Memory lets an assistant remember important facts about you — your preferences, past decisions, or background context — and automatically inject them into future conversations. Instead of re-explaining yourself every time you start a new chat, the assistant already knows what matters. How memory works When memory is enabled, Nexora's configured fast model monitors the conversation and extracts facts worth remembering — things like your name, your preferred coding language, or dietary restrictions. Those facts are stored as discrete memory entries. Before each new conversation, the relevant entries are injected into the context, giving the assistant a head start. Memory extraction runs through the fast model you have configured in Settings → Models . Choose a quick, low-cost model for this role to keep extraction fast and inexpensive. Enabling memory Open the assistant Go to Settings → Assistants and tap the assistant you want to configure. Open the Memory tab Inside the assistant detail screen, tap the Memory tab. Toggle Memory on Enable the Memory switch. The assistant will begin extracting and storing facts from new conversations. Memory settings enableMemory boolean default: false Master switch for memory. When off, no facts are extracted and no memories are injected into conversations. useGlobalMemory boolean default: false When enabled, this assistant reads from and writes to the shared global memory pool rather than its own private store. Only available when Memory is turned on. enableRecentChatsReference boolean default: false When enabled, the assistant can reference a summary of your recent past conversations, giving it broader continuity beyond individual memory entries. enableTimeReminder boolean default: false Injects a time-interval reminder into the context so the assistant is aware of how much time has passed since your last interaction. Global vs. assistant-isolated memory By default each assistant maintains its own private memory store, so facts learned by one persona do not leak into another. Enable Use Global Memory if you want facts to be shared across all your assistants. This is useful when you have several assistants that all need to know the same things about you — your name, time zone, or ongoing projects — without duplicating entries. Setting Behaviour Use Global Memory off Facts are stored privately and are only visible to this assistant Use Global Memory on Facts are stored in a shared pool visible to all assistants that also h

## Prompt Injections and Lorebooks Explained
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/assistants/prompt-injection.html
Automatically insert context snippets into conversations using mode injections and lorebooks, with full control over position, priority, and triggers.

 Prompt injections are snippets of text that Nexora automatically inserts into a conversation's context at a position you choose. They let you augment any assistant with additional instructions, reference material, or world-building lore — without cluttering the main system prompt. Lorebooks extend this idea by grouping multiple injection entries and activating each one only when specific keywords appear in the conversation. Core concepts Mode Injection A manually toggled snippet. Enable it on an assistant and it is always injected whenever that assistant is active. Ideal for "modes" like a formal writing style or a step-by-step reasoning format. Lorebook A named collection of entries. Each entry carries keywords; when those keywords appear in recent messages, the entry's content is automatically injected. Perfect for world-building reference material or project glossaries. Injection positions Every injection targets a specific location in the message list. Choose the position that best matches the intent of your content. Before System Prompt Inserts the content immediately before the existing system message. Use this for high-priority framing that should precede all other instructions. After System Prompt Appends the content to the end of the system message. This is the most common position — it extends the system prompt without replacing it. Top of Chat Places the content just before the first user message in the conversation history. Useful for setting scene context that appears once at the start. Bottom of Chat Inserts the content immediately before the most recent user message. Good for reminders or dynamic context that should be fresh in the model's attention. At Depth Inserts at a specific depth from the end of the message list (e.g., depth 4 = four messages from the bottom). Use this for precise placement relative to recent conversation turns. Creating a mode injection Open Settings Tap the settings icon from the main screen. Navigate to Prompts Select Prompts (also accessible from the Extensions tab of an assistant via the Go to Prompts button). Add a mode injection Tap + in the Mode Injections section. Give it a name, write the content, choose an injection position, set a role (User or Assistant), and assign a priority. Save Tap Save . The injection is now available to attach to any assistant. Creating a lorebook Open Settings → Prompts Navigate to the Lorebooks section and tap + to create a new lorebook. Name the lorebook Give it a descriptive n

## Set Up MCP Servers in Nexora for External Tool Access
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/extensions/mcp.html
Add and configure MCP servers in Nexora to give your AI assistants access to external tools, APIs, and real-world data sources on Android.

 Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI models securely access external tools, APIs, and data sources. Nexora implements MCP as a first-class feature, so you can wire up any compliant MCP server and immediately expose its tools to your assistants — from web search and code execution to database queries and custom business logic. Adding an MCP Server Open MCP Settings Navigate to Settings → MCP . You'll see a list of all configured servers along with their current connection status (Idle, Connecting, Connected, Reconnecting, or Error). Tap Add Server Tap the + button in the top-right corner. Choose the transport type that matches your server. Configure the server Fill in the server details (see Transport Types and Server Options below), then save. Wait for connection Nexora connects automatically and syncs the list of tools the server exposes. A green Connected indicator confirms the handshake succeeded. If the connection drops, Nexora retries automatically with exponential back-off before marking the server as errored. MCP servers must be publicly reachable on the internet or on the same local network as your Android device. Servers behind a firewall or corporate VPN require a VPN connection on the device before Nexora can reach them. Transport Types Nexora supports two MCP transport mechanisms. Both require only a URL endpoint — choose whichever your server advertises. SSE (Server-Sent Events) The original MCP transport. The client opens a persistent HTTP connection and the server pushes events over it. Provide the full SSE endpoint URL, for example https://mcp.example.com/sse . Streamable HTTP The newer, recommended transport defined in the MCP spec. Uses standard HTTP requests with chunked streaming. Provide the base URL of the server, for example https://mcp.example.com/mcp . Server Options Each server has a set of common options you configure when adding or editing it. name string required A human-readable display name for this server. Appears in the MCP server list and in the assistant settings picker. enable boolean default: true Toggle this server on or off without deleting it. When disabled, Nexora closes the connection and does not expose the server's tools to any assistant. url string required The full URL of the MCP endpoint. For SSE servers this is typically a path ending in /sse ; for Streamable HTTP servers it is the base MCP path. headers list of key-value pairs Custom HTTP headers sent with every request to this serv

## Skills: Reusable Capability Bundles for Assistants
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/extensions/skills.html
Bundle prompt instructions into reusable skills you can install once and enable on any Nexora assistant, then share or import via GitHub.

 Skills are self-contained bundles of instructions and configuration that extend what an assistant can do. Think of a skill as a plug-in you install once and then enable on any assistant you like. A skill might teach an assistant how to write in a specific style, follow a domain-specific reasoning process, or call a particular set of tools — all defined in a single portable package that you can share, import from GitHub, or author yourself. Browsing and Managing Skills Open Settings → Extensions → Skills to see all the skills installed on your device. Each card shows the skill's name, a short description, and — if the author included one — a compatibility note indicating which models or providers it works best with. Import from GitHub Tap + and choose Import from GitHub . Paste a repository URL such as https://github.com/owner/repo . Nexora downloads the skill files directly from the repository's default branch. Import from File Tap + and choose Import from File . Select a .zip archive or a plain text file from your device. Nexora extracts the skill and adds it to the list. Create Manually Tap + and choose Add Manually . Paste in the skill content directly — Nexora reads the YAML frontmatter to extract the skill's name and description automatically. Delete a Skill Tap the ⋮ menu on any skill card and choose Delete . Nexora removes the skill from every assistant that had it enabled. Skill File Format Every skill is built around a SKILL.md file that Nexora reads when loading the skill. The file starts with a YAML frontmatter block followed by the instruction body. --- name: code-reviewer description: "Performs thorough code review with style and security feedback" compatibility: "Works best with GPT-4o, Claude 3.5+" allowed-tools: read_file, search --- You are an expert code reviewer. When given a code snippet or file, you: 1. Check for logic errors and edge cases 2. Identify security vulnerabilities 3. Suggest style improvements aligned with the project's conventions ... Frontmatter fields Field Required Description name ✅ Unique identifier for the skill. Must be non-empty and URL-safe. description ✅ One-line summary shown on the skill card. compatibility ✗ Free-text hint about which models or providers work best. allowed-tools ✗ Space-separated list of tool names this skill is designed to use. Viewing and Editing a Skill's Files Tap any skill card to open the Skill Detail page. You'll see a collapsible file tree showing every file inside the skill director

## Workspace
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/extensions/workspace.html
A lightweight Linux environment for AI to handle agent tasks like file editing and creating presentations.

 Workspace provides a lightweight Linux environment for AI, enabling it to manipulate files and complete tasks such as editing files, creating presentations, and more. An assistant can be bound to one workspace. Quick Start Create a Workspace Go to Settings → Extension Management → Workspace to open the workspace management page. Tap the plus button in the bottom-right corner to create a new workspace and enter a name. Tap the newly created workspace card to enter its management page, then tap Install Rootfs to install the system files. Workspace names must be in English. Manage and Configure On the workspace management page, you can: Configure whether tools provided by the workspace require user approval before execution Tap the Files tab to manage workspace files, including importing and exporting Tap the icon in the top-right corner to open the terminal Use in Chat Go back to the chat page and tap the plus button in the chat bar. You will see a card for binding a workspace — tap it to bind to your target workspace. Once bound, the AI can operate within the workspace to complete various tasks when you give it instructions. Glossary Term Description Workspace An isolated Linux environment provided by Nexora for AI. Each workspace runs independently with its own filesystem and packages. Terminal A built-in command-line interface within the workspace where you can run Linux commands to manage files, install software, or debug issues. Rootfs Short for Root Filesystem — the base system files required for a workspace to run. Installing Rootfs is like installing an operating system for the workspace. Installing Common Packages Workspaces use the apt package manager by default. You can install packages manually via the terminal, or let the AI install what it needs during a task. Essential Tools Python Node.js (nvm) Package Purpose curl Send HTTP requests and download files unzip / zip Extract and create ZIP archives git Version control and repository cloning jq Parse and process JSON data apt update && apt install -y curl unzip zip git jq apt update && apt install -y python3 python3-pip Install Node.js via nvm for easy version management: curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.3/install.sh | bash After installation, reload the environment and install Node.js: source ~/.bashrc && nvm install --lts In most cases you don't need to install packages manually — when you give the AI a task, it will automatically install any dependencies it needs. Configure TTS and ASR providers in Nexora to have AI responses read aloud and dictate your messages with a microphone instead of typing.

 Nexora ships with built-in support for both Text-to-Speech (TTS) — hearing AI responses read aloud — and Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) — dictating your messages with a microphone instead of typing. You configure each capability independently, choosing from several cloud and on-device providers. Once set up, TTS and ASR work directly from the chat screen without leaving the conversation. Navigate to Settings → Speech to access both tabs. Text-to-Speech (TTS) Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) Setting Up TTS Open the TTS tab inside Settings → Speech . Tap Add Provider and select the provider you want to use. Fill in the required fields, then tap Save. You can add multiple providers and switch between them at any time. Produces natural-sounding speech with a choice of six preset voices. apiKey string required Your OpenAI API key. Find this in your OpenAI dashboard . baseUrl string default: https://api.openai.com/v1 Base URL for the OpenAI-compatible API. Change this if you are routing through a proxy or using a third-party OpenAI-compatible endpoint. model string default: gpt-4o-mini-tts The TTS model to use. gpt-4o-mini-tts is fast and cost-effective; swap in tts-1-hd for higher fidelity output. voice string default: alloy Voice preset. OpenAI offers alloy , echo , fable , onyx , nova , and shimmer . Gemini TTS Uses Google's Gemini multimodal TTS. Supports a wide range of voices including the expressive Gemini 2.5 family. apiKey string required Your Google AI Studio API key. baseUrl string default: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta Base URL for the Gemini API. model string default: gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts Gemini model to use for speech synthesis. voiceName string default: Kore Voice name. Refer to the Google AI voice list for all available options. MiniMax TTS High-quality Chinese and multilingual TTS from MiniMax. apiKey string required Your MiniMax API key. baseUrl string default: https://api.minimaxi.com/v1 MiniMax API base URL. model string default: speech-2.6-turbo TTS model identifier. voiceId string default: female-shaonv Voice ID. Browse available voices in the MiniMax console. emotion string default: calm Emotional tone of the synthesized voice, e.g. calm , happy , sad . speed float default: 1.0 Playback speed multiplier.  Nexora includes a dedicated image generation workspace that lets you turn text prompts into images — or supply a reference image and ask the model to edit it. Gallery Browse every image you have generated across all sessions, with the prompt and model name displayed on each card. Generating an Image from a Text Prompt Write your prompt Type a descriptive text prompt in the input field at the bottom of the Generate tab. Number of images — generate between 1 and 4 images in a single request. Aspect ratio — choose Square, Landscape, or Portrait. Tap the send button Tap the circular arrow button. Control how Nexora looks: enable Material You dynamic color, switch dark or AMOLED mode, pick a preset theme, build a custom palette, and tune display.

 Nexora gives you full control over how the app looks and feels. You can let Android automatically generate a color scheme from your wallpaper, choose from a curated set of built-in themes, or design a completely custom palette using an HSL color picker. Display options let you adjust font size, message density, code block behavior, and much more — all stored locally on your device. Color and Theme Dynamic Color Dynamic Color automatically generates Nexora's entire color scheme from your current wallpaper using Android's Material You system. When you change your wallpaper, Nexora's accent colors update to match. Dynamic Color requires Android 12 or later. On older devices the toggle is hidden and Nexora falls back to the selected preset or custom theme. To enable Dynamic Color: Open Settings Tap the Settings icon from the main screen. Go to Preferences → Theme Select Preferences , then tap Theme . Toggle Dynamic Color on Enable the Dynamic Color switch. Nexora's UI immediately adopts your wallpaper-derived palette. When Dynamic Color is active, preset and custom theme selections are ignored. Disable Dynamic Color to use them. Dark Mode and AMOLED Dark Mode Nexora follows your system dark/light mode preference by default. You can also enable AMOLED Dark Mode for a true-black background that saves battery on OLED screens. To enable AMOLED Dark Mode: Open Settings → Preferences → Theme Navigate to Settings → Preferences → Theme . Enable AMOLED Dark Mode Toggle on AMOLED Dark Mode . The background switches to pure black in dark mode. Preset Themes Nexora ships with five hand-crafted themes. Each theme has a dedicated light and dark color scheme that is fully accessible and meets Material You contrast guidelines. Sakura Soft pinks inspired by cherry blossoms. The default theme. Ocean Cool blues and teals drawn from deep water. Spring Fresh greens evoking new growth and clear skies. Autumn Warm ambers and earthy tones of the fall season. Black High-contrast dark-first palette optimized for AMOLED. To apply a preset theme: Disable Dynamic Color Preset themes are only available when Dynamic Color is off. Open Settings → Preferences → Theme → Theme Settings Tap Theme Settings to open the theme picker. Select a preset Tap any preset theme tile. The app updates immediately — no restart required. ## Access Nexora's Chat Interface from Any Browser on Your LAN
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/settings/web-access.html
Run a local HTTP server inside Nexora so you can use the full chat interface from any desktop or mobile browser on the same Wi-Fi network.

 Nexora can run a lightweight HTTP server directly on your Android device. Once the server is running, any browser on the same local network — your laptop, a tablet, or another phone — can open the Nexora chat interface without installing anything. The app stays on your phone; the web UI is just a window into it. The web server only works while Nexora is running on your Android device. Closing or force-stopping the app shuts the server down. A persistent foreground notification keeps the server alive when the app is in the background. Starting the Server Open Web Access settings In Nexora, go to Settings → Web Access . Configure the port Enter a port number in the Port field. The default is 8080 . Use any value between 1024 and 65535. You cannot change the port while the server is already running. Choose network visibility Toggle Localhost Only if you want the server accessible only from the device itself (useful for ADB port forwarding). Leave it off to allow access from other devices on your Wi-Fi network. Set an access password (recommended) Enter a password in the Access Password field. See Securing the server below. Start the server Tap the Start button. Nexora requests notification permission and, on Android 15 and later, local network permission, then starts the server. Finding the Server URL Once the server is running, the Web Access page shows the available addresses: Address type When shown Example LAN Address Localhost Only is off http://192.168.1.42:8080 mDNS Address Localhost Only is off, mDNS available http://android-device.local:8080 Local Address Always http://localhost:8080 Tap any address row to copy it to your clipboard. A toast confirms the copy. Open the URL in any browser on the same network. The mDNS address ( .local ) is easier to type and works reliably on most home networks without knowing the device's IP. If it doesn't resolve, fall back to the LAN Address. Securing the Server If you expose the server beyond localhost (i.e. Localhost Only is disabled), anyone on your local network can reach the chat interface. Set an access password to prevent unauthorized access to your conversations and AI provider keys. Nexora uses JWT-based authentication to protect the server: Enter an access password Type a password in the Access Password field on the Web Access settings page. Enable JWT authentication Toggle on Enable JWT Auth . This toggle becomes available once you have entered a non-empty password. Clearing the password automatically di

## Back Up and Restore Your Nexora Conversations and Settings
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/settings/backup.html
Export conversations and settings to a local file, sync automatically to WebDAV or S3-compatible storage, and set reminders so you never lose your data.

 Nexora stores all your conversations, settings, and provider configurations on-device. Use the Backup page to protect that data: export a portable ZIP file for manual safekeeping, push incremental backups to a WebDAV or S3 server, or schedule reminders that prompt you to back up regularly. Navigate to Settings → Backup to get started. The Backup page is organized into four tabs: WebDAV , S3 , Import/Export , and Reminder . Manual Import / Export The Import/Export tab lets you create a complete snapshot of your data and restore it whenever you need — no cloud account required. Export your data Open Settings → Backup → Import/Export Tap the Import/Export tab. Tap Export Tap the Export item under Local Backup / Export . The system file picker opens. Choose a save location Navigate to a folder — local storage, an SD card, or a connected cloud drive — and confirm. Nexora saves a ZIP file containing your full database and associated files. Import from a backup file Tap Import Tap the Import item under Local Backup / Export . The system file picker opens filtered to .zip files. Select your backup ZIP Locate and tap the backup file you previously exported. Restart Nexora After a successful restore Nexora shows a restart prompt. Tap Restart to apply the restored data. Manual export is the recommended method for migrating to a new Android device. Copy the ZIP file to the new device via cable, Bluetooth, or a file-sharing app, then import it. Import from other apps Nexora can also import conversation history exported from other AI chat apps. Chatbox Cherry Studio Tap Import from Chatbox , then select the .json export file produced by Chatbox. Nexora parses the conversation format and merges the history into your local database. Tap Import from Cherry Studio , then select the .zip export file. Nexora extracts and converts the Cherry Studio backup format automatically. WebDAV Sync The WebDAV tab connects Nexora to any WebDAV-compatible server for automatic cloud backup and restore. WebDAV sync is compatible with Nextcloud , ownCloud , and any server that implements the WebDAV protocol — including many NAS devices. Configure the WebDAV connection Open Settings → Backup → WebDAV Tap the WebDAV tab on the Backup page. Enter the server URL Paste your WebDAV endpoint URL into the Server Address field. For Nextcloud, this is typically https://your-server.com/remote.php/dav/files/username/ . Enter credentials Fill in your Username and Password . For Nextcloud, generate a ded

## مرحبًا بك في Nexora — تطبيق دردشة بالذكاء الاصطناعي لأندرويد
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/ar/introduction.html
Nexora تطبيق أندرويد أصلي يجمع OpenAI وGoogle Gemini وAnthropic Claude وأي مزوّد متوافق مع OpenAI في واجهة واحدة أنيقة.

يجمع Nexora كل مزوّدي الذكاء الاصطناعي الكبار في تطبيق أندرويد واحد متقن. بدل التنقل بين تطبيقات وتبويبات متصفح متعددة، تربط مفاتيح API الخاصة بك مرة واحدة وتتحدث مع OpenAI وGoogle Gemini وAnthropic Claude أو أي واجهة متوافقة مع OpenAI من الواجهة المألوفة نفسها. بُني Nexora بلغة Kotlin وJetpack Compose، فيبدو سريعًا وسلسًا ومنسجمًا تمامًا مع جهازك. ابدأ من هنا تنزيل Nexora ثبّت Nexora من صفحة الإصدارات على GitHub وابدأ خلال دقائق. ← البدء السريع أضف أول مزوّد، واختر نموذجًا، وأرسل أول رسالة في أقل من خمس دقائق. ← مزوّدو الذكاء الاصطناعي اربط OpenAI وGoogle Gemini وAnthropic Claude أو أي واجهة API متوافقة مع OpenAI. ← المساعدون أنشئ مساعدين مخصصين بتعليمات نظام ونماذج وشخصيات خاصة بك. ← إضافات MCP وسّع إمكانيات Nexora عبر أدوات بروتوكول سياق النموذج (MCP). ← الوصول عبر الويب افتح واجهة محادثة Nexora من متصفح على شبكتك المحلية. ← لماذا Nexora؟ صُمم Nexora حول فكرة واحدة: تجربتك مع الذكاء الاصطناعي يجب أن تكون ملكك. تستخدم مفاتيح API الخاصة بك، وتختار نماذجك، وتحتفظ بخصوصية محادثاتك. بلا اشتراكات ولا وسطاء ولا قيود على الانتقال. مزوّدون متعددون في تطبيق واحد بدّل بين OpenAI وGemini وClaude والواجهات المتوافقة دون مغادرة التطبيق. ← مساعدون مخصصون ابنِ مساعدين قابلين لإعادة الاستخدام بتعليمات نظام ونماذج وشخصيات مختلفة. ← دعم أدوات MCP اربط أدوات ومصادر بيانات خارجية عبر بروتوكول سياق النموذج. ← بحث مباشر على الويب فعّل الوصول اللحظي للويب لتبقى إجابات الذكاء الاصطناعي دقيقة وحديثة. ← يستند Nexora إلى RikkaHub (رخصة AGPL-3.0). هذا التوثيق مقتبس من توثيق RikkaHub المنشور برخصة MIT — راجع LICENSE .

## تثبيت Nexora على أندرويد
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/ar/download.html
نزّل ملف Nexora APK من إصدارات GitHub، واختر النسخة المناسبة لجهازك، وأكمل إعداد أول تشغيل.

Nexora تطبيق أندرويد أصلي يُوزَّع كملف APK من صفحة إصدارات المشروع على GitHub. تشرح لك هذه الصفحة التنزيل والتثبيت وإكمال أول تشغيل. متطلبات النظام ℹ️ يعمل Nexora على هواتف وأجهزة أندرويد اللوحية. لا توجد نسخة لنظام iOS. التنزيل افتح صفحة الإصدارات اذهب في متصفحك إلى صفحة إصدارات Nexora . اختر الملف المناسب يحتوي كل إصدار على عدة ملفات APK: الملف متى تستخدمه app-arm64-v8a-release.apk معظم الهواتف الحديثة (معالج 64 بت). app-armeabi-v7a-release.apk الهواتف الأقدم ذات المعالج 32 بت. app-x86_64-release.apk المحاكيات والأجهزة ذات شريحة x86. app-universal-release.apk يعمل على كل ما سبق، لكن حجم الملف أكبر. إذا لم تكن متأكدًا من الملف المناسب لجهازك، فاستخدم النسخة الشاملة (universal). ثبّت ملف APK افتح الملف الذي نزّلته من مدير الملفات. إذا طُلب منك ذلك، فعّل Install unknown apps للمتصفح أو مدير الملفات، ثم اتبع التعليمات على الشاشة. ⚠️ نزّل Nexora من المستودع الرسمي المذكور أعلاه فقط. ملفات APK من مصادر أخرى قد تكون قديمة أو معدّلة. ℹ️ للتحديث، ثبّت ملف APK أحدث فوق التطبيق الحالي. الإصدارات موقّعة بالمفتاح نفسه، لذا تبقى بياناتك محفوظة. تجربة أول تشغيل بعد تثبيت Nexora افتحه من الشاشة الرئيسية أو قائمة التطبيقات. في أول تشغيل يرشدك Nexora خلال الإعدادات الأساسية: شاشة الترحيب يستقبلك Nexora بشاشة ترحيب قصيرة. اضغط Get Started للانتقال إلى الإعداد. أضف مزوّدًا يطلب منك Nexora إضافة مزوّد ذكاء اصطناعي واحد على الأقل. اختر مزوّدك المفضل — OpenAI أو Google Gemini أو Anthropic Claude أو واجهة مخصصة متوافقة مع OpenAI — وأدخل مفتاح API. يمكنك إضافة مزوّدين آخرين لاحقًا من Settings ← Providers . اختر نموذجًا افتراضيًا اختر نموذجًا افتراضيًا للمحادثات الجديدة. يمكنك تغيير النموذج لكل محادثة في أي وقت. ابدأ الدردشة اضغط Start Chatting لفتح شاشة المحادثة الرئيسية. Nexora جاهز للاستخدام. استيراد إعدادات المزوّد عبر رمز QR إذا كنت قد هيّأت Nexora على جهاز آخر، فيمكنك تخطي إدخال مفاتيح API يدويًا باستيراد إعدادات المزوّد برمز QR. كيفية الاستيراد عبر رمز QR على جهازك الحالي: افتح Settings ← Providers . اضغط خيار Export أو Share واختر QR Code . سيظهر على الشاشة رمز QR يحتوي إعدادات المزوّد. على جهازك الجديد: أكمل التثبيت وافتح Nexora. في شاشة إعداد المزوّد اضغط Import via QR Code . وجّه الكاميرا إلى رمز QR على جهازك الحالي. يستورد Nexora إعدادات المزوّد تلقائيًا. ℹ️ يتضمن رمز QR مفاتيح API الخاصة بك. أبقِه سريًا ولا تشاركه علنًا ولا تلتقط له لقطة شاشة وتحفظها في مكان غير آمن. الخطوات التالية دليل البدء السريع أضف مزوّدًا وأرسل أول رسالة في أقل من خمس دقائق. ← نظرة عامة على المزوّدين تعرّف على إعداد OpenAI وGemini وClaude والواجهات المخصصة. ←

## البدء السريع: أرسل أول رسالة للذكاء الاصطناعي في 5 دقائق
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/ar/quickstart.html
ثبّت Nexora على أندرويد، واربط أول مزوّد ذكاء اصطناعي بمفتاح API الخاص بك، واختر نموذجًا، وأرسل أول رسالة في أقل من خمس دقائق.

يوصلك هذا الدليل من الصفر إلى أول محادثة مع الذكاء الاصطناعي بأسرع طريقة. تحتاج إلى جهاز أندرويد مثبّت عليه Nexora ومفتاح API من مزوّد واحد على الأقل. إذا لم يكن لديك مفتاح بعد، فسجّل لدى المزوّد الذي تختاره أولًا. نزّل Nexora وثبّته ثبّت Nexora على جهاز أندرويد من صفحة الإصدارات على GitHub. إصدارات Nexora (GitHub) نزّل أحدث ملف APK من صفحة إصدارات المشروع. ← بعد اكتمال التثبيت افتح Nexora من الشاشة الرئيسية أو قائمة التطبيقات. افتح الإعدادات وأضف مزوّدًا يحتاج Nexora إلى مزوّد ذكاء اصطناعي واحد على الأقل قبل أن تتمكن من الدردشة. انتقل إلى إعدادات المزوّدين الآن. اضغط أيقونة Settings (الترس) أسفل الشريط الجانبي. اختر Provider Settings من قائمة الإعدادات. كثير من المزوّدين مهيّؤون مسبقًا — إن وجدت مزوّدك فاضغط عليه وأدخل مفتاح API. وإلا فاضغط الزر في الزاوية العلوية لإنشاء مزوّد جديد. OpenAI Google Gemini Anthropic Claude أكثر صيغ API انتشارًا. أدخل عنوان Base URL ومفتاح API من مزوّدك لإكمال الإعداد. لدى OpenAI إصداران من API. Chat Completions هو الافتراضي في Nexora وهو الأكثر شيوعًا وتدعمه غالبية المزوّدين. أما Responses API الأحدث فهو ما تمنحه OpenAI الأولوية الآن — فإذا كنت تستخدم واجهة OpenAI الرسمية أو وسيطًا يحاكي نماذج GPT فيُنصح بالتحويل إليه. اضغط Use Responses API لتفعيله. صيغة API الخاصة بـ Google، وتُستخدم حصريًا مع نماذج Google Gemini. ثاني أكثر صيغ API اعتمادًا بعد OpenAI. يستخدمها Claude وعدد من النماذج الأخرى أيضًا. أدخل مفتاح API الصق مفتاح API في حقل API Key للمزوّد الذي اخترته. إذا كنت تستخدم وسيطًا غير رسمي وغير مدمج في Nexora، فستحتاج أيضًا إلى ضبط Base URL عند إنشاء المزوّد. ⚠️ تعامل مع مفتاح API كأنه كلمة مرور. لا تشاركه ولا تلصقه في تطبيقات غير موثوقة. يحفظ Nexora مفتاحك محليًا على جهازك ولا يرسله أبدًا إلى خوادم Nexora — بل يذهب مباشرة إلى المزوّد الذي اخترته. بعد لصق المفتاح اضغط Save أو Confirm لحفظ إعدادات المزوّد. أضف النماذج بعد ضبط المزوّد، مرّر إلى قسم Models أسفل شاشة المزوّد واضغط عليه. يدعم معظم المزوّدين جلب قائمة النماذج تلقائيًا — اضغط زر التوسيع لتحميل القائمة ثم اختر النماذج التي تريدها. لحذف نموذج لم تعد بحاجة إليه، اسحبه للحذف. ℹ️ يمكنك تغيير النموذج في أي وقت من داخل المحادثة عبر منتقي النموذج في شريط أدوات الدردشة. اضبط النماذج الافتراضية ارجع إلى صفحة الإعدادات واختر Default Models & Prompts لتحديد النموذج الافتراضي لكل ميزة. إلى جانب نموذج الدردشة، يمكن لميزات أخرى (مثل توليد العناوين والتلخيص) أن تستخدم كل منها نموذجًا مختلفًا — وغالبًا ما يؤدي نموذج أسرع وأرخص عملًا جيدًا في هذه المهام. ابدأ أول محادثة كل شيء جاهز. ارجع إلى الشاشة الرئيسية وابدأ محادثة جديدة. اضغط زر اختيار النموذج أسفل الشاشة لاختيار النموذج الذي تريده. اكتب رسالتك الأولى في حقل النص واضغط Send . يبثّ Nexora الرد إليك لحظة بلحظة. هذا كل شيء — أنت جاهز! 💡 جرّب بداية بسيطة مثل «اشرح لي ما الذي يمكنك مساعدتي فيه» لتتعرف على قدرات النموذج قبل الانتقال إلى مهام أكثر تحديدًا. ⚠️ تجنّب سؤال النموذج عن هويته. فالنماذج لا تملك وعيًا دقيقًا بهويتها — وهذه خاصية أساسية في طريقة عمل النماذج اللغوية الكبيرة وليست خللًا في Nexora. تستطيع التطبيقات الرسمية الإجابة بشكل صحيح لأنها تحقن تعليمات نظام تخبر النموذج بهويته. لا يتضمن Nexora هذه التعليمات افتراضيًا، لكن يمكنك إضافتها بنفسك من إعدادات تعليمات النظام. ماذا تستكشف بعد ذلك نظرة عامة على المزوّدين أضف مزوّدين آخرين وتعلّم الخيارات المتقدمة مثل عناوين Base URL والترويسات المخصصة. ← المساعدون المخصصون أنشئ مساعدين قابلين لإعادة الاستخدام بتعليمات نظام ونماذج افتراضية وشخصيات خاصة. ← إضافات MCP اربط أدوات ومصادر بيانات خارجية ليتمكن الذكاء الاصطناعي من تنفيذ إجراءات حقيقية. ← الوصول عبر الويب فعّل البحث المباشر على الويب ليجيب الذكاء الاصطناعي عن الأحداث والمعلومات الحديثة. ←

## مزوّد OpenAI — GPT وسلسلة o والواجهات المتوافقة
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/ar/providers/openai.html
اضبط مزوّد OpenAI في Nexora لاستخدام GPT-4o ونماذج الاستدلال من سلسلة o أو أي واجهة متوافقة مع OpenAI بتحكم كامل في مفتاح API والعنوان.

يربط نوع المزوّد OpenAI تطبيق Nexora بواجهة Chat Completions أو Responses من OpenAI. ولأن بروتوكول OpenAI أصبح معيارًا في الصناعة، فإن نوع المزوّد نفسه يعمل مع عشرات الخدمات الخارجية — يكفي تغيير عنوان Base URL. تركّز هذه الصفحة على الاتصال المباشر بـ OpenAI؛ وللإعدادات الخارجية والمحلية راجع المزوّدين المخصصين / المتوافقين مع OpenAI . أضف مزوّد OpenAI افتح إعدادات المزوّدين انتقل إلى Settings ← Providers واضغط Add Provider . اختر OpenAI اختر OpenAI من قائمة أنواع المزوّدين. أدخل مفتاح API الصق مفتاح OpenAI API في حقل API Key . يمكنك العثور على المفاتيح أو إنشاؤها من platform.openai.com/api-keys . تأكد من عنوان Base URL القيمة الافتراضية لعنوان Base URL هي https://api.openai.com/v1 . اتركها كما هي للاتصال القياسي بـ OpenAI. أضف النماذج اضغط Add Model ، وأدخل معرّف النموذج (مثل gpt-4o أو o3 )، واضبط اسم العرض والقدرات، ثم احفظ. كرّر ذلك لكل نموذج تريد استخدامه. احفظ اضغط Save لتطبيق التغييرات. سيظهر المزوّد ونماذجه الآن في منتقي النموذج. مرجع الإعدادات الحقول الأساسية apiKey string required مفتاح OpenAI API الخاص بك. يحفظه Nexora محليًا على جهازك ولا يرسله إلا إلى عنوان Base URL المضبوط. يدعم تدوير المفاتيح المفصولة بفواصل (مثل sk-key1,sk-key2 ) عند امتلاكك عدة مفاتيح. baseUrl string default: https://api.openai.com/v1 الرابط الجذر لواجهة API المتوافقة مع OpenAI. غيّره عند الاتصال بوسيط أو بخدمة خارجية تحاكي واجهة OpenAI. chatCompletionsPath string default: /chat/completions المسار الذي يُلحق بعنوان Base URL لطلبات المحادثة. غيّره فقط إذا كان مزوّدك يستخدم مسارًا غير قياسي. الحقول المتقدمة useResponseApi boolean default: false التبديل من نقطة Chat Completions إلى واجهة Responses الأحدث من OpenAI. فعّل هذا للنماذج التي تدعم Responses API فقط، مثل المقدَّمة عبر نقطة Grok من xAI. includeHistoryReasoning boolean default: true عند التفعيل، يضمّن Nexora المحتوى reasoning_content من ردود المساعد السابقة عند إرسال سجل المحادثة. عطّله إذا كان مزوّدك يرفض الرسائل التي تحتوي حقول الاستدلال. التحقق من الرصيد فعّل التحقق من الرصيد لعرض رصيد API المتبقي مباشرة في شاشة تفاصيل المزوّد. balanceOption.enabled boolean default: false شغّل عرض الرصيد لهذا المزوّد. balanceOption.apiPath string default: /credits المسار (نسبةً إلى Base URL) أو الرابط الكامل المستخدم لجلب رصيدك. القيم الشائعة: /credits — OpenRouter /user/balance — DeepSeek /user/info — SiliconFlow balanceOption.resultPath string default: data.total_usage مسار بصيغة النقاط داخل استجابة JSON يشير إلى قيمة الرصيد الرقمية. مثلًا، يُحسب data.total_credits - data.total_usage لـ OpenRouter، و balance_infos[0].total_balance لـ DeepSeek. ترويسات HTTP مخصصة يمكنك إرفاق ترويسات HTTP إضافية بكل طلب يرسله هذا المزوّد. افتح قسم Custom Headers في شاشة تفاصيل المزوّد وأضف أزواج المفتاح والقيمة. هذا مفيد لأنظمة المصادقة التي تتطلب ترويسات إضافية (مثل HTTP-Referer مع OpenRouter) أو للوسطاء في الشركات. حقول مخصصة في جسم الطلب يتيح لك قسم Custom Body حقن حقول JSON إضافية في كل طلب محادثة. استخدمه لتمرير معاملات خاصة بالمزوّد لا يعرضها Nexora كإعدادات أساسية — مثل safe_mode لبعض النقاط المزوّدة بالإشراف أو معاملات أخذ العينات الخاصة بمزوّد معيّن. تحقق من اتصالك بعد الحفظ، افتح شاشة تفاصيل المزوّد واضغط Test Connection . يرسل Nexora طلبًا بسيطًا إلى عنوان Base URL ويخبرك هل قُبل مفتاح API. إذا فشل الاختبار، فراجع مفتاح API وعنوان Base URL. ليست كل الواجهات المتوافقة مع OpenAI تنفّذ مسار قائمة /models . إذا لم يعمل اكتشاف النماذج، فأضف معرّفات النماذج يدويًا بالمعرّف الدقيق الذي يتوقعه المزوّد. مثال: الاتصال بـ OpenRouter عبر النوع OpenAI استخدم نوع المزوّد OpenAI، واضبط Base URL على https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 ، وأضف مفتاح OpenRouter API، واختياريًا أضف HTTP-Referer و X-Title كترويسات مخصصة. راجع المزوّدين المخصصين لشرح كامل.

## مزوّدو الذكاء الاصطناعي — اتصل بخدماتك المفضلة
URL: https://mhamad-code.github.io/Nexora-docs/ar/providers/overview.html
تعرّف على كيفية إضافة عدة مزوّدي ذكاء اصطناعي وضبطهم والتبديل بينهم في Nexora، ومنهم OpenAI وGoogle Gemini وAnthropic Claude والواجهات المخصصة.

يتيح لك Nexora الاتصال بعدة خدمات ذكاء اصطناعي في الوقت نفسه، فتختار النموذج المناسب لكل محادثة دون مغادرة التطبيق. يُسمّى كل اتصال تضبطه مزوّدًا (provider) — ويحفظ مفتاح API وعنوان Base URL وأي خيارات إضافية لازمة للتحدث مع خدمة ذكاء اصطناعي معيّنة. يمكنك إضافة ما تشاء من المزوّدين، وتفعيل كل واحد أو تعطيله على حدة، والتبديل بين نماذجهم مباشرة من شاشة المحادثة. أنواع المزوّدين المدعومة يدعم Nexora أصلًا ثلاثة أنواع من المزوّدين، إضافةً إلى خيار مخصص مرن يعمل مع أي واجهة متوافقة مع OpenAI. OpenAI اتصل بواجهة OpenAI — بما فيها GPT-4o ونماذج الاستدلال من سلسلة o وواجهة Responses API — أو بأي خدمة تحاكي نقطة Chat Completions. Google Gemini استخدم نماذج Gemini مباشرة عبر Google AI API، أو استخدم Vertex AI بحساب خدمة للنشر في المؤسسات. Anthropic Claude تحدّث مع نماذج Claude عبر Anthropic API، مع تخزين مؤقت اختياري للأوامر (prompt caching) لتقليل زمن الاستجابة والتكلفة في المحادثات الطويلة. مخصص / متوافق مع OpenAI وجّه Nexora إلى OpenRouter أو نسخة Ollama محلية أو وسيط مستضاف ذاتيًا أو أي خدمة أخرى تتحدث بروتوكول OpenAI Chat Completions. أضف أول مزوّد افتح Settings اضغط أيقونة Settings في شريط التنقل السفلي لفتح شاشة الإعدادات. انتقل إلى Providers اختر Providers من قائمة الإعدادات لعرض كل المزوّدين المضبوطين. أضف مزوّدًا اضغط Add Provider ، واختر نوع المزوّد، واملأ مفتاح API وأي حقول مطلوبة أخرى، ثم احفظ. أضف النماذج داخل شاشة تفاصيل المزوّد، أضف معرّفات النماذج التي تريد استخدامها. يظهر كل نموذج في منتقي النموذج عند بدء محادثة أو التبديل بين النماذج. إدارة عدة مزوّدين يمكنك ضبط ما تحتاجه من المزوّدين. استخدم مفتاح التبديل في بطاقة كل مزوّد لتفعيله أو تعطيله دون حذف إعداداته. المزوّدون المعطّلون ونماذجهم تُخفى من منتقي النموذج. إذا أردت مقارنة ردود مزوّدين مختلفين، فأضف كل واحد على حدة وبدّل النماذج بين المحادثات — دون إعادة إدخال بيانات الاعتماد. شارك إعدادات المزوّد برموز QR في شاشة تفاصيل كل مزوّد زر Share يحوّل إعداد المزوّد (مفتاح API وBase URL والإعدادات — دون أي نماذج مضافة) إلى رمز QR. يستطيع مستخدم Nexora آخر مسح الرمز لاستيراد الإعداد نفسه فورًا. ويمكنك أيضًا نسخ النص المشفّر وإرساله عبر أي تطبيق مراسلة. رمز QR ونص المشاركة يحتويان مفتاح API الخاص بك. شاركهما فقط مع من تثق بهم، وألغِ المفتاح من لوحة تحكم المزوّد إذا انكشف يومًا. التحقق من الرصيد المزوّدون الذين يدعمون نقطة للرصيد أو الأرصدة يمكنهم عرض رصيدك المتبقي في شاشة تفاصيل المزوّد. فعّل Balance Checking في إعدادات المزوّد وحدّد مسار API ومسار الحقل في JSON الذي يحمل قيمة الرصيد. راجع صفحات المزوّدين الفردية لأمثلة خاصة بكل مزوّد. بعض المزوّدين يحجبون الطلبات من دول أو مناطق معيّنة. إذا ظهر لك خطأ رفض وصول أو 403 فجرّب مزوّدًا آخر.
